questions.answer: Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) is a strategic framework for making sure your brand appears in AI-generated search results and recommendations. It involves optimizing your digital footprint so AI systems recognize your brand as authoritative, relevant, and trustworthy enough to cite [6]. Compared with AEO, GEO is broader and longer term, focusing on being recognized as a trusted entity that AI systems mention by name [5]. The site notes that it also depends on solid technical SEO, since AI search tools find content through the same basic mechanisms as traditional crawlers [8].

questions.answer: A GEO strategy needs technical SEO as its foundation. Without it, AI systems may not be able to crawl your content, discovered pages may not be indexed for AI retrieval, and slow, insecure or mobile-unfriendly pages may be deprioritized [2]. The basics include making sure AI crawlers can reach your pages, that important content renders in the HTML, and that pages are indexed [3]. Schema markup, fast and secure pages, and clear site architecture also help AI systems extract and trust your content [2][7]. Joe's AEO program covers these areas as AI crawler rules, server-rendered content, llms.txt and page speed [4]. For questions about working with Joe, see the [contact page](/contact/).

questions.answer: Keyword research now centers on user intent and conversational queries rather than search volume alone [1][4]. Start by identifying the specific problems your audience wants to solve, and use tools with intent classification to analyze patterns like SERP features and related keyword clusters [3][4]. Joe also suggests studying the "People Also Ask" section and reviewing how people search on platforms like Reddit, not just Google [4][5]. Covering topics thoroughly with related subtopics fits this approach [7]. For help applying this to your own site, see [the contact page](/contact/).
